items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: He also taught I think this guy's name is Albert Pick, who was -- he's quite a guitarist, he's quite a classical guitarist.

ctx.x: Everything -- Frank -- and they didn't spell my teacher's name. His name was Lanham. He was a very marvelous -- he was a marvelous man. Frank Lanham. I'll tell you, I studied with this man in Chicago, and he wanted to teach me classical guitar, and I didn't want to play classical guitar, and I wouldn't -- I wouldn't take classical guitar so he taught me the Electrum style. And you couldn't -- you had to write, you see, when you studied with him you had to also write. He taught you really the fundamentals of…

But I -- he never knew how old the classical guitar was until I started studying with him, and so I was there taking a lesson one day, and an old black man came in, this guy looked like he was about 80. He was -- well, he was in his eighties. Very stately and well groomed, and he and Mr. Lanham started talking and it was very interesting to hear them talk. They had toured Europe. I forgot this guy's name, playing the classical guitar. Years before. Now this was in the thirties, you know, and I was amazed, because…
